record.paper_title: Recent developments and open problems in the theory of permanents
record.original_question: Let D_n be the set of n-tuples (A_1,...,A_n) of n x n positive semidefinite matrices such that trace(A_i)=1 for every i and A_1+...+A_n=I. Which elements of D_n are extreme points of this convex set?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n\geq 2$ and let $D_n$ denote the set of all $n$-tuples $(A_1,\ldots,A_n)$ of complex (or real) $n\times n$ positive semidefinite matrices such that
\[
\operatorname{tr}(A_i)=1 \quad\text{for every } i=1,\ldots,n, \qquad \text{and}\qquad A_1+A_2+\cdots+A_n=I_n,
\]
where $I_n$ is the $n\times n$ identity matrix. The set $D_n$ is convex. Characterize explicitly the extreme points of $D_n$: that is, give a description of all tuples $(A_1,\ldots,A_n)\in D_n$ with the property that whenever $(A_1,\ldots,A_n)=\tfrac{1}{2}(B_1,\ldots,B_n)+\tfrac{1}{2}(C_1,\ldots,C_n)$ with $(B_i),(C_i)\in D_n$, one must have $B_i=C_i=A_i$ for all $i$.
artifact.category_tag: Extreme points of matrix convex sets
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return a definitive characterization of the extreme points of the convex set $D_n$ of $n$-tuples of $n\times n$ PSD matrices of trace one summing to the identity. Related results exist on extreme points of correlation matrices and matrix convex sets, but no source clearly resolves this specific problem, which is identified as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Extremal correlation matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Characterization of rank-k extreme points of related PSD convex sets, with rank bound k(k+1) ≤ 2n.
status_evidence.claim: Related but distinct convex sets of PSD matrices have known extreme-point characterizations, but not the specific set D_n in question.

status_evidence.title: Extreme points of matrix convex sets
status_evidence.snippet: General theory of matrix extreme points and free spectrahedra.
status_evidence.claim: General machinery exists, but does not directly resolve the explicit characterization for D_n.
